dog.description_text:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Totis is at risk due to behavior concerns. He has not acclimated well to the care center environment and has shown highly fearful and defensive behavior during his stay. Initially shut down, he has stiffened, hard barked, growled, and bared teeth at handlers when being leashed and when removed from kennel. His previous owners report that he barks and growls at unfamiliar people who approach his family or home, and has some handling sensitivity including snapping when his paws are touched. Outside of this, his previous owners describe him as an independent, active, and playful dog who prefers contact on his own terms but is affectionate once comfortable. Medically, Totis is apparently healthy.

Totis was surrendered due to his family moving out of the country. His previous family described him as an independent, active, playful, yet lazy dog who prefers contact on his own terms. He spends most of his time in the bedroom, kitchen, or living room of his home and pulls moderately on his leash during his two daily walks. He is very affectionate once he is comfortable, and he loves going on car rides. He primarily ate dry food at his last home and is not picky with toys or treats. His owners did note that he has escalated to hard barking and growling at strangers and will snap when his paws are touched. Similar behaviors have been displayed during his stay in care. Totis has not acclimated well and is not allowing for minimal handling. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.
